title: VPC / On‑Prem Compliance Talk Track and GTM Notes
content:
Purpose:
A concise selling and technical talk track for VPC and on‑prem offers aimed at regulated customers (finance, healthcare, gov). This doc is a lightweight GTM note to be used by AE, pre-sales, and product marketing while we iterate on the more formal one‑pager and enablement deck.

Audience / personas: 
- Procurement / Legal: cares about contractual guarantees (data residency, indemnity, breach notification).
- Security / InfoSec: cares about encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM integration, auditability, penetration testing, SOC/ISO evidence.
- Platform / Infra: cares about network topology, egress controls, latency, upgrade paths, observability hooks.
- Line‑of‑Business / Product: cares about time‑to‑market, predictable latency, and avoidance of vendor lock‑in.

Core positioning pillars (short statements to use verbatim):
- Private hosting with a customer‑managed control plane option: keep orchestration and audit control inside your VPC while we provide the inference runtime you ship against.
- Compliance by design: configurable data flows, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit trails to map to regulatory controls (HIPAA, FINRA, GDPR).
- Production economics with isolation: dedicated capacity and policy controls so regulated apps get predictable latency and transparent unit costs.
- Graceful fallbacks & ops safety: policy-driven routing and automatic downgrade paths to ensure uptime during maintenance or capacity events.

Quick 30‑second elevator pitch (customer facing):
"Redwood can run inside your VPC or on‑premise so sensitive data never leaves your environment. We deliver the same high‑throughput inference runtime teams rely on in our hosted API, plus controls for encryption, audit logs, and upgrade governance that make compliance audits straightforward."

Competitive shorthand (how to differentiate vs other options):
- Managed cloud vendors: they offer convenience but often lack fine-grained customer control of the orchestration plane and baked-in private networking options; emphasize our customer‑controlled plane and local KMS integration.
- Self‑hosted open‑source runtimes: lower initial license cost but require heavy engineering lift for secure multi‑tenant operations, autoscaling, and long‑tail maintenance; position Redwood as "managed runtime + ops patterns" that removes that burden.
- Specialized compliance vendors: might solve one regulatory checkbox (e.g., FedRAMP), but they often don't provide inference‑specific optimizations (KV cache, batching) — highlight our production‑grade perf with compliance features.

Opponent map (short list of likely competitors & primary counter messaging):
- Major cloud AI endpoints (A, B): "They have scale but limited ability to give you the management plane in your network. Ask: who controls encryption keys and upgrades?"
- Inference infra startups (X, Y): "Ask about their operational guarantees and observability for token‑level costs — can they prove throughput SLAs under your workload shape?"
- Internal build: "We help quantify the total cost of ownership — engineering hours, security reviews, and SRE ops to match our SLA are usually underestimated."

Objection handling (short scripts):
- "We can't let vendor code run inside our network." -> "We provide a private control plane mode where orchestration components are customer‑owned; the runtime processes are constrained to nodes you manage and we provide signed binaries + SBOMs and reproducible upgrade manifests."
- "Who owns the keys?" -> "Customer KMS/HSM first: you control keys, we never persist plaintext training or sensitive payloads outside configured memory windows. We support popular KMS providers and HSM for customers that require FIPS 140‑2/3."
- "What about audit evidence?" -> "We export immutable audit logs, access trails, and model version history that you can forward to your SIEM. We can provide artifact bundles for audits (logs + manifests + test prompts)."
- "If performance matters, won't on‑prem slow us down?" -> "Our runtime adapts kernel choices and batching for your hardware; we provide reference hardware profiles and perf baselines, plus a lab validation run before go‑live."

Technical clarifications / safe answers for pre‑sales engineers: 
- Data residency: All customer payloads are written only to ephemeral memory unless configured for persistent storage; persistent stores map to customer provisioned volumes.
- Control plane variants: (1) Fully hosted control plane (no PII leaves Redwood), (2) Customer‑managed control plane inside VPC (recommended for regulated customers), (3) Offline/on‑prem package for air‑gapped environments.
- Upgrades & rollouts: support canary rollouts pinned by model version and region; customers can opt into manual approval gates for major model changes.
- Observability: token‑level tracing, per‑route cost breakdown, and exportable tracing hooks (OpenTelemetry).

Pricing and contracting cues:
- Typical elements to expect in RFP: pilot term (3‑6 months), dedicated capacity commitment (monthly GPUs / vCPUs), compliance addendum (data processing addendum + security appendix), audit support hours.
- Pricing knobs to use in negotiation: committed capacity discounts, on‑call SLA credits, longer term support retainer vs ad‑hoc support hours.
- ROI bullets (talk to CFO/procurement): reduced engineering lift vs build, predictable per‑token unit economics at scale, fewer incident hours due to integrated fallbacks.

Open questions / risky assumptions to validate with customers:
- Customers occasionally require vendor attestation beyond SOC/ISO (e.g., specific FedRAMP package) — need legal confirmation if we can support without additional engineering.
- Some regulated customers demand application‑level logging redaction controls — confirm product roadmap for field‑level redaction.
- Pricing expectations for on‑prem appliances (we've not released standard list pricing).

One‑page checklist for an AE call with a regulated prospect: 
1) Confirm deployment desire: hosted | customer VPC | on‑prem air‑gapped.
2) Ask where keys must live and which KMS/HSM vendor they use.
3) Ask for compliance frameworks in scope (HIPAA, SOC2, PCI, FINRA, FedRAMP).
4) Ask for perf needs (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec) and sample prompt length.
5) Offer lab validation and perf baseline as next step.
6) Share audit artifact sample and SBOM on request.

Next steps / owners:
- Product marketing: convert this into a trimmed one‑pager and an AE deck by 2024‑11‑15 (owner: Maya).
- Presales: prepare a short demo script for customer‑managed control plane by 2024‑11‑01 (owner: Owen).
- Legal: draft a compliance appendix template we can attach to MSA for pilot customers (owner: Lucas).

Notes / unresolved snippets: 
- Collect two anonymized customer examples of on‑prem migration success for case studies.
- Need legal to confirm the language we can use around "we never see customer data" for customer‑managed control plane mode.
- Verify glossary: make a clear distinction in collateral between "control plane" (orchestration + policy) and "data plane" (runtime nodes) to avoid misunderstandings.

Slack threads / embeds to follow up: #priv-deployments, #gtm-product, #pre-sales

End of draft.
